newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo share jump puts focus on chance of rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo share jump puts focus on chance of rate rise.

text.p: Tokyo stock market resumed its bull run on Tuesday after a long weekend, with a key index climbing to its highest levels in four months spurred by Wall Street's advance and investors' bidding for blue-chip shares.

Traders said the unexpectedly robust rally had increased expectations of an early end to Japan's ultra-soft monetary policy, capping the dollar's rise against the yen and triggering a sell-off in Japanese government bonds.

The benchmark Nikkei average of 225 leading shares soared above the psychologically important 20,000 level soon after the opening. It was the first time the Nikkei had topped 20,000 since December 19.
"Stocks rallied almost across the board," said Kunihiro Hatae, general manager at Tokyo Securities Co Ltd.
The Nikkei finished the morning session at 20,204.52, up 689.77 points or 3.53 percent from its Friday close. June Nikkei futures jumped 710 points to 20,240.
The rally capped the dollar's upside at around 126.50 yen and triggered a jump in Japanese long-term interest rates, traders said.

They said speculation was growing that the stock market's strength would take pressure off Japan to keep its current ultra-soft monetary policy, as it would benefit the fragile banking and other financial sectors.
The yield of the benchmark 10-year Japanese government bond had risen 10 basis points by midday to 2.4 percent. The key June 10-year futures had fallen more than a full point to 124.33.
The dollar stood at around 126.00 yen at midday.

"Worries over downside risks have diminished recently, and the surge in U.S. stocks lifted the Nikkei 225 more steeply than expected," said Hisao Suzuki, deputy general manager at Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd.

On Monday, the Dow Jones Industrial average closed above 7,200 points for the first time ever on hopes that a balanced federal budget deal would keep the U.S. Federal Reserve from raising interest rates later this month.
The Dow closed up 143.29 points or two percent at 7,214.49. It was one of the biggest point gains ever for the 30-share average, and other market averages also set records.
In Tokyo, active investor bidding for blue-chip issues led the market's overall rally, with shares in electronics giant Sony Corp hitting a record high on Tuesday.

Sony soared as high as 9,510 yen soon after the opening, surpassing a previous high of 9,500 yen marked in October 1989 during Japan's economic "bubble" of sky-high stock and asset prices. The share stood at 9,490 yen at midday.

Other Japanese blue-chip shares such as Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd, Hitachi Ltd and NEC Corp also rose. They were helped by the recent weakness of the yen, which makes their products more competitive abroad, brokers said.

Brokers said the market was supported by hopes that cash-rich public pension funds would continue to hunt for shares of blue-chip companies whose earning are likely to benefit from the yen 's recent weak trend.
Foreign investors also appeared to be showing a healthy interest in buying Japanese stocks, which have lagged behind recent strong rally in American shares, brokers said.
Despite the recent gains, some remained sceptical about the possibility of further advances.

"Unless there are fresh fundamental factors, shares are unlikely to rally further in the face of prevailing strong caution about the topside," said an official at a second-tier Japanese brokerage. ($1=126 yen)
